run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: The request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 resolves to one log record in the log catalog: an ERROR at 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z in index app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05, service "auth", region "eu-west", response_time_ms 15847, whose text reads "Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts." So the service with the issue is auth in Europe (eu-west): the request took ~15.8 s instead of the 150 ms that every other sampled auth request in that region and the same-period samples in ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, us-east and us-west show, and authentication failed after retries, which is what the customer's error page reflects. Affected (own evidence): the auth service in eu-west (its own ERROR record with 15847 ms). Checked and not showing any latency or error deviation: the other 26 services in the EU indices (20 docs each, max 150 ms, 0 ERROR) and the five other regions (270 docs each, max 150 ms); the cluster's pods (32 pods, none non-Running; otel-demo's 22 pods Running with restartCount 0) and deployments (24, all available/ready/updated = 1) show no restart or availability damage, but their application-level error/latency signals could not be read because Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable in this Run. The LDAP backend that the record blames is named only in that message; no LDAP-specific telemetry, workload or pod exists to inspect, so what exhausted its connection pool remains an open hypothesis rather than an observed fact.

claims.text: The only record containing REQ-EU-8K4M2 in the whole log catalog (1620 indices matching app-185-geo-*, whole authorized window) is _index app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05, @timestamp 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z, level ERROR, service "auth", region "eu-west", response_time_ms 15847, message: "Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts." (match_phrase total 1, 1620/1620 shards successful).

Comparable baseline for the same service and region: app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-* holds 11 documents between 2026-11-14T19:29:00Z and 2026-11-23T19:29:00Z; ten are level INFO "Request completed successfully" with response_time_ms 150 (one per day), and the single exception is the 15847 ms ERROR record for REQ-EU-8K4M2 at 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z.

Auth is the only service in the EU indices with an ERROR bucket and the only one whose response_time_ms exceeds 150: auth 21 docs (eu-west + eu-central), 1 ERROR, avg 897.5 ms, max 15847 ms, while each of the other 26 services (analytics, api, billing, cache, cart, catalog, checkout, db, inventory, notification, orders, payments, pricing, profiles, promotions, ratings, recommendations, reviews, search, shipping, subscriptions, tracking, users, web, wishlist, worker) has 20 docs, 0 ERROR and max exactly 150 ms.

Auth by region over the whole authorized window: eu-west 11 docs, avg 1577 ms, max 15847 ms; ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, us-east and us-west 10 docs each with max exactly 150 ms — the deviation is confined to eu-west.
Region-level aggregate over all 1620 indices: eu-west 271 docs, avg 207.9 ms, max 15847 ms; ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, us-east and us-west 270 docs each with avg and max exactly 150 ms.

A catalog-wide search over app-185-geo-* for level ERROR, level WARN, or messages containing "timeout" or "exhausted" across the authorized month matched exactly one document: the same eu-west auth record at 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z with 15847 ms.

In the 2-hour window 2026-11-18T15:30:00Z–17:30:00Z across the 540 EU indices, the only document logged at all is this auth ERROR record; no other service logged a record around the failure time (match_all, total 1).

Kubernetes state at query time shows no workload or pod identity for "auth" or an LDAP backend: the complete deployment list (24 objects, all namespaces) contains no auth/ldap deployment and the log catalog's 27 service names (analytics … worker) include no ldap service; all 32 cluster pods are Running (no pod matches status.phase!=Running) and otel-demo's 22 pods show restartCount 0.

The only Kubernetes events inside the authorized window are three Warning events from endpoint-controller, reason FailedToCreateEndpoint, involvedObject kind Endpoints name "loki" (services app-101/loki, app-102/loki, app-282/loki) at 2026-11-23T18:39:56Z, 18:50:09Z and 19:12:19Z — five days after the REQ-EU-8K4M2 failure and unrelated to authentication; the namespaces app-101/app-102/app-282 are not readable.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo was read at query time and every declared flag (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) has defaultVariant "off"; this is the value in effect when the query ran, not proof of its value at 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z.

Mechanism, stated by the record itself: the auth service's LDAP backend connection pool was exhausted, so the authentication call waited 15847 ms and the customer's authentication failed after retries. What exhausted the pool (LDAP server latency, pool size/timeouts, bind storms or lockouts) is not observable in any available source — there is no LDAP-side metric, log index, workload or pod.

Considered and rejected: another service or another region of the same application was the slow component for this request. Per-service EU aggregates show only auth above the 150 ms baseline with an ERROR, and the five other regions show max exactly 150 ms, so no other identity has its own slow/error evidence for this window.

Considered and rejected: an otel-demo fault-injection flag (flagd) produced this failure. The record belongs to the app-185 log catalog's "auth" service, which has no deployment or pod in this cluster, while flagd's flags all read "off" at query time and none of the otel-demo service names appears in the record; caveat: the flag values were read after the incident, so this rejection rests on the absence of any link, not on incident-time flag values.

Considered and rejected: the loki FailedToCreateEndpoint events indicate the cause of the customer's slow response. They are Endpoints-controller races on services in namespaces app-101/app-102/app-282 occurring on 2026-11-23, five days after the auth timeout, and concern endpoint creation, not authentication latency.

Have the auth-service owners inspect the LDAP client pool at 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z: pool size and checkout timeout, LDAP server/bind latency, and any bind storm or account-lockout pattern; the record's own diagnostic points there and no other component shows a deviation.

Restore query access to the tracing and metrics backends for this target and re-test: an auth/eu-west latency series from traces_span_metrics_calls_total or rpc_client_duration_milliseconds (and an LDAP-side signal) would quantify blast radius, which the current 1-document-per-service-per-day log sampling cannot.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services, traces_search (frontend, 18:31–19:31Z and 19:00–19:31Z on 2026-11-23) and traces_list_operations (frontend) all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace for REQ-EU-8K4M2 exists in this evidence set — the call path, parent/child edges and per-span durations are unknown.

Prometheus was unreachable: get_metric_names ({__name__=~"traces_.*"}, {__name__=~"http_.*"}), get_label_values (status_code on traces_span_metrics_calls_total), get_prometheus_target, metrics_range_query and execute_prometheus_instant_query (up; sum(up); sum by (service_name) increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total...)) all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate or latency series could corroborate the log record or cover the otel-demo services' own signals.

The LDAP backend named in the record is unidentifiable in this evidence: no metric, label, log index (the catalog has 27 services, none ldap/directory), deployment or pod represents it, so its health at 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z is unknown.

The auth service has no Kubernetes workload: no configmap, deployment, pod, status, event or container termination reason for auth could be read, and secrets (any credential used for the LDAP bind) cannot be read, so an authentication-configuration cause could not be verified.

Application stdout logs could not corroborate the record: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-6c9bc688bf-ll8s7, frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-q7f5n and prometheus-readonly-proxy-7567c75596-nwrxw returned 0 lines/0 bytes in the query window (no_data), including the previous-instance stream being unavailable.

Log coverage is sparse and short: the app-185-geo-* documents observed span only 2026-11-14T19:29:00Z–2026-11-23T19:29:00Z with ~1 document per service per day per region, so whether other requests were also slowed (blast radius) before, during or after 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z is unknown; the month before that sampling is unobserved.
Whether an LDAP pool setting, credential or auth configuration changed shortly before 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z cannot be checked: the change_history integration is not configured for this Run.

The three events name services app-101/loki, app-102/loki and app-282/loki in namespaces that are not readable in this cluster (namespace list contains only default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo), so those objects remain unread gaps.
next_steps: Obtain the auth service's own metrics and traces (and its LDAP server's) for 2026-11-18T16:40–17:10Z once the Prometheus and Jaeger backends are reachable again.
Ask the auth/LDAP owners for LDAP connection-pool size, checkout wait time and bind latency around 2026-11-18T16:52:47Z, and check whether the pool limit was ever reached before or after.

Confirm the customer-facing blast radius from the web/error-page side (how many distinct request IDs failed with authentication errors in that minute) rather than inferring it from the single sampled record.

The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
